_comment: Shared drift vectors for the dual-homed llm.prompt_hash (the cross-service
cache key). This file is byte-identical in CodeRoot-OpenSource and
CodeRoot-Repo-Assessor; both suites assert it, so a divergent copy fails
loudly instead of producing a permanent, silent cache-key mismatch between
the two services.
DERIVED BY EXECUTION: every `sha256` below was produced by calling the real
`prompt_hash(system, user, schema_name)` in CodeRoot's
coderoot_oss/llm/cache.py. Two of them -- 'separator_pair_a' and
'order_asymmetry' -- were additionally cross-checked BY HAND against
System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256 (.NET, not Python/hashlib) over a
manually constructed byte string following the documented layout
`f"{schema_name}\x1f{system}\x1f{user}"`, so this fixture pins the
algorithm the docstring describes, not merely whatever the code happened
to emit.
What each case guards against:
- separator_pair_a / separator_pair_b: without the \x1f separator,
'ab'+'c' and 'a'+'bc' concatenate to the same string ('sabc' after the
schema_name prefix), so a refactor that drops or changes the separator
collapses these two DIFFERENT (system, user) pairs onto the SAME hash.
Their recorded digests must differ.
- order_asymmetry: the function signature is
`prompt_hash(system, user, schema_name)` but the interpolation order is
`schema_name, system, user` -- schema_name comes FIRST in the string even
though it is the LAST argument. Three distinct values (alpha/beta/gamma)
make a refactor that interpolates in argument order instead produce a
different, non-matching digest.
- empty_* : boundary behaviour when one or more fields are the empty string.
- non_ascii: UTF-8 encoding correctness for non-Latin scripts, accents and
an emoji (astral-plane codepoint).
- control_and_quote_chars: embedded quotes, newlines and a tab must not be
escaped/altered before hashing.
